review_method: Read-only review previously completed; this receipt adds no source reading, build or test execution.

findings.finding: Opaque FunctionBodyRevision follows existing same_body proof: actual declaration bytes, parser attribute context, file/ordinal binding and FunctionLowerBinding. It is neither a hash nor prior Typed result authority.

FunctionLowerBinding binds temporary count and, when used, module temporary start. Node-derived $discard naming marks node_named and requires unchanged function NodeId before body input identity can survive.

Gap reconciliation retains complete input context, namespace, target/full limits, owner, location and name checks. Row, retained Typed function and signature table must agree on the concrete FunctionId.
Typed FunctionId is declaration offset plus ordinal; Builder receives that explicit ID rather than copying CoreFunction.id.

Changed raw NodeId enters binding Work even when body token and span are unchanged. The consumer updates Row.node and input revision, preserving the next continuous delta binding; changed positions retain original rebase path.
Scalar admission excludes template/closure/resource expression and nonprimitive shape domains relevant to additional NodeId consumers.
Fresh Builder state and Typed result remain subject to push_closed_state and closed_function checks.
Inspected statement NodeId bookkeeping is conditional on managed/owned/closure resources, outside the retained primitive result domain.

nearest_counterexamples: A prior edit shifts raw nodes before an unchanged let _ binding: its actual $discard name changes, so node_named requires a changed body revision and fresh Types.
An unchanged body consumes module-global generated temporaries after an earlier edit: changed temporary start/count prevents retaining its body revision.
Raw NodeId changes with identical span and body: omitting binding Work would leave Row.node stale and break the next continuous delta; this implementation explicitly updates it.
limits_of_conclusion: No equivalence claim for arbitrary Core, templates, closures or resource identity domains
No relaxation of independent Verify, full user limits or successful-publication requirements
No independent runtime validation performed by this reviewer
